dedupe_keys.name: can ale canadian active living environments index by dissemination area 2006 2011 2016 2021

description: Can-ALE, the Canadian Active Living Environments database, scores how friendly every Canadian neighbourhood is to walking, cycling and transit use, for research on how the built environment relates to physical activity. The 2.0 update by Meisam Ghasedi and Daniel Fuller (University of Saskatchewan) with Gorham Achot and Nancy A. Ross (Queen's University) rebuilt the whole data and code pipeline and adds the 2011 and 2021 census years to 2006 and 2016. For each Dissemination Area, measures are computed within a 1 km circle around the population-weighted centroid: population and dwelling density from the census, transit stops from GTFS feeds (2016 and 2021 only), density of intersections with three or more legs from the Statistics Canada road network file, and weighted points of interest such as schools, libraries and hospitals from OpenStreetMap; walk-to-work and active transport to work shares are added for 2011 to 2021. Coverage: all Dissemination Areas in Canada for four census years. Access: one CSV per year and open R code on GitHub, with the 2019 version 1.0 files and user guides in English and French; postal-code linked data come through CANUE under a data sharing agreement. Licence: no licence file is stated; the authors ask for citation of the user manual; free. Caveats: the authors warn against longitudinal comparison because OpenStreetMap completeness and transit data differ between years; some Dissemination Areas lack dwelling counts. Simulation uses are neighbourhood walkability inputs for activity, mobility and health models and for public space planning. Related records: the OpenStreetMap leisure and park features record; the transport piece holds Can-BICS.
